subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — recap & next steps

Thanks for taking the call earlier, Sarah — quick recap and next steps to validate Dedicated capacity for Acme's search/QA workload.

Call highlights:
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 150ms for streaming responses (chunked token streaming), p50 <= 60ms for non-streaming; sustained throughput target ~300 req/min with occasional spikes to 500 req/min; typical concurrency ~40–60 concurrent requests.
- Model profile: 13B encoder-decoder model with 1k token average responses; heavy use of streaming and partial response display in UI.
- Compliance: data-in-transit only; we'll run validation in your VPC-connected Dedicated environment.

Initial sizing guidance (high level):
- Baseline: 4x NVIDIA A100 (80GB) reserved pool — should meet throughput at conservative batching and KV-cache enabled.
- Performance tier: 2x H100 (80GB) for better p95 latency and lower cost-per-token when using aggressive batching.
- Cost/throughput tradeoff: H100 reduces per-token latency but has higher per-hour cost; we'll provide a detailed perf matrix.

Proposed validation plan:
1) You provide sample payloads & typical concurrency profile (see attached sample_payloads.json).
2) We provision a short Dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) for a 2–4 hour run in your VPC.
3) Run a baseline A100 test, then an H100 comparison; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token rate, and error rate.
4) We review results and recommend final sizing and reserved throughput.

Next steps:
- Please confirm available dates for a perf window next week (we have availability Tues/Wed 10–14 PT).
- Share sample payloads and any special streaming shaped traffic.

Attachments: redwood_perf_matrix_v1.pdf (high-level sizing), sample_payloads.json (example requests)

Thanks,
Aditya
Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — recap & next steps

Thanks, Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifications before we lock a window:

- The 300 req/min is our steady-state (search queries). Spikes to 500 coincide with hourly batch jobs hitting the front-end, so we'd like the system to sustain that for ~10 minutes without degradation.
- Concurrency probably peaks at ~60, but average is ~25. Many requests are short (<200 tokens) but 15–20% return ~600–800 tokens.
- Streaming is important — we stream partial answers to the UI; p95 streaming latency matters more than p50.

Questions:
1) For the baseline A100 configuration you suggested, what batching strategy will you use and how will you preserve low tail latency while batching?
2) Do you have any recommendations on KV cache sizing for our average 1k-context workload?

We can do Tue (16 Mar) 10–12 PT for a 2-hour run; would prefer H100 if cost allows.

On sharing payloads — I'll drop a redacted dataset to the Drive link you shared by EOD today.

—Sarah
Director, Search Engineering
Acme Retail

Thanks — Tue 16 Mar 10–12 PT works. We're happy to provision H100s for the run. Quick answers to your questions below and a short checklist for the perf run.

1) Batching & latency:
- We'll use dynamic continuous batching with a 15–20ms coalescing window tuned for low tail latency and flow-based limits to avoid queueing during spikes. For streaming, we maintain small micro-batches per token generation to keep partial-token latency low.

2) KV cache sizing:
- For a 1k-context average with 15–20% long responses, I recommend starting with 48–64GB of shared KV cache per GPU; we can adjust after initial runs. We'll capture hit rates and miss patterns during validation.

Perf run checklist:
- Acme to upload redacted sample payloads to the Drive link.
- Provide expected concurrency timeline (CSV or simple summary).
- Confirm VPC peering info and any IP allowlists.
- Approve provisional provisioning: 2x H100 (80GB) reserved for a 2-hour validation window on Tue 16 Mar 10–12 PT.

I'll put in the provisioning request and send calendar invites once I have your confirmation and the sample payloads.

Cheers,
Aditya
